name: Lesending
author: 老蒋和他的小伙伴

sections.description:
Lesending lets you choose a publish target while editing: local site only, local plus remote, or remote only (after a successful sync the local post is saved as a draft and the mode resets to local only).

This plugin is developed by Lezaiyun Studio and maintained by LaoJiang.

Official product page: https://www.lezaiyun.com/lesending.html

Developer blog: https://www.laojiang.me

Connection modes

  • REST + Application Passwords: for sites with a working WordPress REST API. The plugin auto-detects /wp-json, /index.php/wp-json, and index.php?rest_route= endpoints.
  • Bridge file: when remote REST is restricted, upload a standalone PHP bridge to the remote WordPress root and authenticate with a shared secret.

Editor

  • Gutenberg sidebar panel
  • Classic editor meta box
  • Sync log meta box with per-site results

Media sync

  • Toggle image sync in plugin settings
  • When enabled, content images and the featured image are uploaded to the remote media library and URLs are rewritten
  • Supports REST media upload and bridge sideload

Settings

  • Card-style remote site list
  • Connection test for REST and bridge modes
  • Bridge script download (optional custom .php filename)

Uninstalling the plugin removes options and related post meta (see uninstall.php).
sections.installation:
1. Upload the lesending folder to /wp-content/plugins/.
  2. Activate Lesending under Plugins.
  3. Go to Settings → Lesending, enable remote publishing, and add remote sites.
  4. For bridge mode: download the bridge script, upload it to the remote WordPress root (same folder as wp-config.php), set the secret and user ID, then enter the bridge URL and the same secret on this site.
sections.faq:
What does REST mode require on the remote site?

The remote site must be WordPress, with Application Passwords enabled for a user who can publish posts. The REST API must not be fully blocked by a security plugin. For plain permalinks (index.php?rest_route=), the plugin tries to discover the REST entry automatically.

When should I use bridge mode?

Use the bridge when remote REST is unavailable, blocked, or returns 404. Upload the downloaded bridge file (or a custom .php name) to the remote site root, set LESENDING_BRIDGE_SECRET and LESENDING_BRIDGE_USER_ID, and enter the same secret in Lesending settings.

Which images are synced?

Only images from this site’s uploads directory (wp-content/uploads), including content images, block images, and the featured image. External CDN or third-party URLs are not downloaded. Up to 30 images per post.

How do I disable image sync?

Uncheck “Sync images” under Settings → Lesending, or use the lesending_sync_media filter in code.
sections.changelog:
1.1.2

  • Plugin Check compliance: English readme, languages folder, bridge shipped as downloadable template with ABSPATH-protected stub.
  • Admin download uses WP_Filesystem; stricter input sanitization; settings view variable prefixes.

1.1.1

  • Security hardening: remote sync requires publish_posts; credentialed requests use wp_safe_remote_* with no redirects; HTTPS required by default.
  • Credential storage upgraded to AES-256-GCM (legacy ciphertext still supported); public editor site list no longer exposes remote usernames.
  • Bridge: minimum 32-char secret, explicit user ID, optional IP allowlist, sideload limits, minimal ping payload.

1.1.0

  • Sync content images and featured image to the remote media library (REST upload / bridge sideload).
  • Settings toggle for image sync.
  • Bridge refactor: validate secret before loading WordPress; improved ping and error JSON.
  • REST discovery for index.php?rest_route= and Link header parsing.
  • Card-style settings UI; connection tests can reuse a saved bridge secret.

1.0.0

  • Initial release: REST sync, three publish modes, block editor sidebar, settings page, and uninstall cleanup.
